method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, formula and reference comparison, reverse paraphrase and structural QA. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The formal inductive definition of primitive recursive functions, its stage construction, proofs for addition and multiplication, and reduction of the exponential example to the basic functions.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Primitive recursion turns k-place f and (k+2)-place g into a (k+1)-place h; composition turns k-place f and k many n-place component functions into an n-place h. Zero, successor and projections are basic, and the class is closed under those two constructions.
samples.checks: Every arity, index range, base/successor equation and five defining clauses are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Equivalently, the primitive recursive functions form the least set containing zero, successor and projections and closed under composition and primitive recursion. A stage construction starts with those functions and repeatedly applies one construction; the union over natural-number stages is the class.
samples.checks: Leastness, closure, one-step stage formation and the union formula are all retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Addition is primitive recursive because its recursion uses identity/projection for the zero clause and a three-place g obtained by composing successor with the third projection.
samples.checks: The proposition and proof preserve every reference, projection index, arity distinction and displayed equation.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Multiplication is primitive recursive; its proof is assigned as an exercise asking the reader to fit the known definition into the primitive-recursion scheme and verify f and g.
samples.checks: The proposition label, exercise placeholder and problem's two required tasks remain distinct and intact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The h(y)=2^y example first adds a dummy argument because the formal scheme requires k at least 1. Constant 1 comes from Succ composed with Zero; doubling comes from multiplication, a constant-2 helper and projections. A final composition removes the dummy argument.
samples.checks: All helper functions f, g, g-prime, g-double-prime and h-prime, their nesting, constants and projection indices are preserved exactly.

source_observations: OLCMP-003 documents the frozen title's 'Primitive Recursion Functions' wording; आदिम पुनरावर्ती फलने matches the function class repeatedly and formally defined in the body.
T302 supplies the established primitive-recursive class name; T288 and T053 separately supply primitive recursion and composition.
T119 supports विगमनाधारित व्याख्या, T101 supports the explicit 'closed under' phrasing, and T207 controls every arity label.
T253 and T051 support प्रक्षेपण, एकरूपता फलन and स्थिर फलन in the addition and exponential reductions.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
